subject: Autoscales overlay pricing & cooldown exit clause - ACME Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Autoscales overlay pricing & cooldown exit clause - ACME Dedicated commit

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Per our conversation attached is a concise pricing proposal for the Dedicated commit + autoscale overlay you asked about. The goal is to provide a predictable baseline (reserved commit) and a clearly priced add-on for burst/autoscale that preserves your latency SLOs during spikes.

High-level summary:
- Reserved commit: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (zonal) guaranteeing 600 tokens/sec sustained throughput.
- Autoscale overlay (burst add-on): up to 2x of the committed capacity for short windows (burst cap = 200% of base). Billed as a per-minute surge rate, with a 30-minute rolling cooldown applied after sustained burst usage.
- Surge rate: $X per GPU-minute (see attached workbook for tiered slabs and effective blended rates based on 12/24/36 month terms).
- Discounting: standard volume discounts apply on the reserved commit; we can offer a one-time overlay volume credit if ACME commits 24 months.

Two items you flagged for procurement: explicit cooldown exit clause (ability to request an emergency cooldown exception during a verified outage) and a clear SLA on throughput during overlays. We can add an "overlay exception" provision to allow one verified cooldown override per 12 months with jointly-agreed verification (service incident + customer telemetry).

Attached: acme_burst_pricing_v3.pdf (proposal) and redwood_capacity_slab.xlsx (per-minute modeling).

Would love your feedback on the cooldown exception language and whether the 200% burst cap maps to your operational needs. If helpful, we can model a capped-IOPS alternative (token-based instead of GPU-based) — that tends to be cheaper for short, very high-QPS bursts.

Next step: if this lane looks right, I can convert to a redline-ready term sheet and loop in Legal.

Cheers,
Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: acme_burst_pricing_v3.pdf (PDF, 1 page summary), redwood_capacity_slab.xlsx (Excel workbook, pricing model)

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscales overlay pricing & cooldown exit clause - ACME Dedicated commit

Thanks Lauren —

Appreciate the clear summary and the workbook. A few procurement questions that will determine whether we go 12 or 24 months:
1) Can you clarify how the 30-minute rolling cooldown works for a repeated burst pattern? For example, if we do three 10-minute spikes separated by 5 minutes idle, how will that be billed and how does the cooldown re-arm?
2) If we hit the overlay cap during a major event, is there an automated fallback to a lower-cost model variant (e.g., quantized variant) or will requests be queued/failed? We need an SLA-backed behavior.
3) On the overlay exception: procurement will want objective verification steps and a timeline for exception approval (we can't have multi-day approval in an outage).

Also: we need a list of proof points for your latency guarantees under overlay (traceable examples or runbooks). Can you provide a short appendix for our SREs?

Sarah
Sr. Manager, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscales overlay pricing & cooldown exit clause - ACME Dedicated commit

Hi Sarah —

Below are answers and a slightly revised commercial structure to address the three asks. I put numbers in the workbook (tab: ACME_RUN) and added a short appendix for SRE verification.

1) Cooldown semantics: the 30-minute rolling cooldown starts after a contiguous burst window ends. In your example (three 10-minute spikes separated by 5 minutes idle), the overlay billing would treat the three spikes as a single sustained burst because the idle gaps are less than the cooldown window — so the cooldown would begin after the last 10-minute spike. Billing: per-minute on actual overlay consumption during the burst window. The intent is to prevent repeated micro-bursts from being billed as separate events.

2) Overlay behavior at capacity exhaustion: our default is graceful degradation with prioritized routing (best-effort to compatible quantized variants) + request throttling once overlay capacity is exhausted. For SLA-backed behavior, we can define two options:
   - Option A (Preferred): Automatic fallback to a verified quantized model variant with capped latency SLO (e.g., p95 < 400ms). This requires pre-testing/qualifying the quantized variant.
   - Option B: Hard cap + queuing with a documented retry/reject policy (simpler but higher risk to user-facing latency).

3) Overlay exception process: we can agree a 4-hour expedited review SLA for kickoff of an exception, with one emergency override permitted per 12-month period (requires a joint incident report and a single-point contact ack). If you need more overrides, we can add a paid reserve of emergency credits.

Commercial tweak (proposal): for a 24-month commit we can offer a 15% overlay-rate credit for the first 6 months and reduce the initial cooldown to 20 minutes for the first 3 months as a ramp. The workbook models blended $/GPU-minute across 12/24/36 terms and includes an "emergency credits" add-on as a prepaid bucket.

I've attached the SRE appendix (in the same drive link) and updated the acme_burst_pricing_v3.pdf with the two options above. Happy to schedule a short walk-through with your SREs.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment references: acme_burst_pricing_v3.pdf (v3 includes Option A/B), redwood_capacity_slab.xlsx (ACME_RUN tab)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscales overlay pricing & cooldown exit clause - ACME Dedicated commit

Sarah / Karthik —

Two practical items from ops/legal I'll call out to make contracting smoother:

1) "Cooldown exit clause" language: we propose the following short text for the term sheet: "Customer may request an overlay exception during a verified service incident; Redwood will respond within 4 hours to initiate the exception workflow. One exception may be granted per 12-month period without additional fee; further exceptions may be provided on a prepaid emergency-credit basis." Please confirm if this aligns with Acme's risk tolerance.

2) Metering evidence: for exception approval we require (a) Redwood incident ID, (b) customer telemetry snapshot (5-minute window), and (c) a short joint incident report within 72 hours. This keeps approvals objective and auditable.

If you want the reduced initial cooldown (20 minutes) for the ramp months in writing, I'll add the specific effective dates to the term sheet before we send to Legal.

Soojin
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Autoscales overlay pricing & cooldown exit clause - ACME Dedicated commit

Sarah —

Thanks for the questions. Based on Karthik & Soojin's updates I've attached a redline-ready term summary and included the explicit cooldown exit clause and the two overlay behavior options. Quick recap of the commercial offer for ACME if you go 24 months:
- Reserved commit: 8x A100-equivalents, guaranteed throughput as discussed.
- Overlay: up to 200% of base for up to 60 contiguous minutes; 20-minute cooldown during first 3 months as ramp, then 30-minute rolling cooldown.
- Discount: 15% overlay credit first 6 months, and a 10% committed discount on reserved capacity (reflected in workbook).
- Emergency exception: 1 granted per 12 months; 4-hour response SLA to initiate; metering evidence + 72-hour joint incident report required.

Next steps: if this looks good I can open a HubSpot deal (link below), drop a term sheet into DocuSign, and loop in Legal for a quick redline. If you prefer a 12-month commit we can send a 12-month variant (different discounting) — say the word and we'll prepare both.

Drive deck: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/acme/burst_workbook
DocuSign (term sheet draft): https://docusign.example/ACME-042-term

Best,
Lauren
